## Verbatim quotes (auto-generated captions)

> "We've been posting on YouTube for over 6 years. We've done over 100 million views and grown this channel to 1.3 million subscribers."

> "Till the lifetime of our channel, where we have over a hundred million views on the channel, we have generated $248,963. It feels bad. Over 6 years."

> "Sure, we only made $248,000 from YouTube AdSense, but I will say that we have made more than six times as much money in every other way."

> "And then on August 31st, 2021, we hit 100,000 subscribers. That's when we got our silver play button."

> "So, the next milestone here, we hit 10,000 subscribers in September 8th of 2020."

## Arithmetic used in the post

- $248,963 / (100,000,000 / 1,000) = $2.49 per 1,000 views. The channel reports "over" 100M views, so the true rate is a little lower, and the post says "under $2.50".
- 10,000 views a month = 10 x $2.49, which is about $25.
- $5,000 / $2.49 per 1,000 views = about 2.0 million views.

## Caveat

The transcript says "we hit 1 million subscribers on July 31st of 2020". That date conflicts with the 100,000-subscriber date (2021-08-31) and is likely a slip of the tongue. The post does not use it.
